items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen when walking 10 to 19 minutes after dinner. If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, ask your care team about low sugar before adding walks after meals.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: None of your 2 scored dinners started at 8 pm or later. Keep it that way: across the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a quarter of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Try not to have dinner too late, as sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners in the program. Having dinner before 8 pm is a good idea, as it may help keep sugar levels in check.
